Title: March 12, 2026 City Council Study Session
Overview: The March 12, 2026 study session covered a remembrance declaration, the proposed Downtown Development Authority, and the city's long-term financial and ballot strategy. The council's declaration designating March 22 as Boulder Day of Remembrance for the 2021 King Soopers shooting victims was signed by Mayor Brockett, with a ceremony set for that day. On the DDA, council generally supported further refinement toward a possible November ballot decision, and on ballot measures, straw polls narrowed the options to four, with staff returning in April and May.

Topic1.Title: Boulder Strong Day of Remembrance Declaration
Topic1.Summary: Councilmember Wallach presented a declaration designating March 22 as the Boulder Day of Remembrance to honor the 10 people killed in the March 22, 2021 King Soopers mass shooting. The council read the victims' names and announced a remembrance ceremony at the Boulder Museum on March 22 from 3:30 to 4:30 p.m. The declaration was signed by Mayor Aaron Brockett.

Topic2.Title: Downtown Development Authority Formation and Initial Recommendations
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the proposed Downtown Development Authority, a tax increment financing tool to fund long-term reinvestment in downtown and the Hill, with a study area still under refinement and no final boundaries. Staff recommended exploring a standalone DDA with a 1-2 year transition, a funding model combining a mill levy, property and sales tax increment, and possibly parking assets, with fiscal safeguards. Council asked about voting thresholds, the base year, parking and GID asset transfers, staff costs, liability, and oversight, and generally supported continued refinement toward a November ballot decision.

Topic3.Title: 2026 Ballot Measures and Long-Term Financial Strategy
Topic3.Summary: Finance staff presented the long-term financial strategy, noting that 68% of city revenues are dedicated and that property tax growth has slowed sharply. Staff previewed transformational, mid-range, and structural tax ballot options, including a sales tax on services, a sales-to-property tax swap, a general purpose mill levy, a public realm mill levy, a residential vacancy excise tax, a general fund debt authorization, a mill levy cap increase, and consolidation of dedicated sales taxes. Through straw polls, council narrowed the options to the public realm mill levy, residential vacancy excise tax, general fund debt authorization, and consolidation of dedicated sales taxes, with staff returning in April and May.
